duplicate_or_version_note: The normalized artifact contains the 1986 journal article together with journal cover, editorial, and table-of-contents matter. Duplication or version relationships relative to the frozen parent corpus were not assessed in this source-only pass, so all novelty metadata is unconfirmed.
extraction_risk: High: OCR systematically corrupts inequality signs, Greek letters, derivatives, subscripts, Euclidean-space notation, and many displayed equations; some formulas are incomplete or spatially disordered, and figure and journal-front-matter text is interleaved with the article. Because the counterexample depends on exact PDEs, asymptotic estimates, and closing conditions, semantic extraction requires a cleaner source or manual equation-level verification.
mathematical_scope: Construction of a non-spherical constant-mean-curvature immersion of a torus in Euclidean three-space; reduction of conformal curvature-line surface equations to a sinh-Gordon-type elliptic PDE; reconstruction from Gauss and Mainardi-Codazzi compatibility; reflection symmetries, translational and rotational period-closing conditions; continuation and separation arguments; large Dirichlet solutions, asymptotic analysis, and modified Newton iteration.
usefulness_reason: The source has strong potential for teaching counterexample design: it isolates which hypotheses support earlier rigidity results, converts the geometric target into an integrable PDE, reconstructs geometry from compatibility data, exploits symmetry to reduce closure to period conditions, and combines asymptotic construction with continuity to force a closed immersed torus. It is quarantined rather than rejected because these conceptual moves are valuable, but the normalized text does not preserve the exact formulas and estimates needed to extract them faithfully as mathematical records.
